entities.summary:
Pseudo-Philo, the anonymous author of the Biblical Antiquities, was a key figure in shaping Jewish historiography during the Hellenistic period.


    Written in Hebrew, the text was preserved in Latin and has been transmitted through manuscripts dating from the 11th to the 15th centuries CE.


    The work is significant for its influence on the development of Jewish historiography and its contribution to the creation of a narrative about the origins of the Jewish people.


    Pseudo-Philo's work has also been the subject of scholarly debate and analysis, with some viewing it as a product of Jewish identity formation and others as a reflection of Christian interests.


    As a result of its transmission and reception, the Biblical Antiquities has had a lasting impact on the study of Jewish history and the interpretation of biblical texts.
